prayerExcerpt.en-US: He baptized St. Paulinus in 388, and the latter, in several letters, speaks of him as his father and his master.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Batizou São Paulino em 388, e este, em várias cartas, fala dele como seu pai e seu mestre.

meta.face: A Gallo-Roman of Aquitaine of about sixty-five with a fresh, lightly weathered complexion and a face like a ROUNDED RECTANGLE, EVEN in width from temples to jaw, with STRONG, rounded CHEEKBONES — a moderate forehead under thick grey hair RECEDING at the temples to a marked WIDOW'S PEAK; a PRONOUNCED brow over DEEP-SET, kind blue-grey eyes with fine laughter creases; a SHORT nose, gently SCOOPED in profile, with a rounded, slightly lifted tip; a LONG upper lip; a WIDE, calm mouth with a humorous lift at one corner; a SHORT, full, CURLY salt-and-pepper beard close to the jaw; the look of a father and teacher. Not the clean-shaven, heart-shaped paulinus_nola, the round-bearded nicasius or the lean valery.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book's engraving shows him bearded, with receding hair, teaching the young Paulinus; the face is ours within that, as the fatherly 'father and master' of Paulinus's letters. The shell recalls the baptism of Paulinus; the Roman Bordeaux behind him is the city of his friend Ausonius.
